name: Colorado
overview: Colorado county treasurers sell tax lien certificates on properties with unpaid property taxes. They don't sell the property itself. State law requires the sale on or before the second Monday in December, so most counties hold it in October or November, and the larger counties now sell online through SRI (Zeus Auction) or RealAuction (coloradotaxsale.com). Bidders compete by paying a premium (bonus bid) above the amount due. The premium is never refunded and earns no interest. The lien earns a yearly redemption rate set at nine points above the federal discount rate (13% for 2026 sales, per several counties). If the owner hasn't redeemed after three years, the holder can apply for a Treasurer's deed.

counties.how_to_bid: In person only: you or your agent must be present. Register with the Treasurer's Office on sale day with a W-9 (SSN, or EIN for companies). Each buyer gets a number; raise it to bid and call out your premium. Premiums go in $1 steps on taxes under $1,000 and $5 steps above that, and are not refunded on redemption. The county page states the 2026 rate of return as fourteen percent (other Colorado counties list 13% for 2026, so confirm).
